round_summary.overall_hypothesis: This initial diagnostic round explores a small set of simple, interpretable audio feature families to determine which primitive acoustic directions—spectral shape, energy dynamics, pitch characteristics, and temporal statistics—are most informative for utterance-level sarcasm detection with an RBF SVM, relative to a minimal MFCC baseline.
evidence_used: The dataset is 690 utterance-level audio samples from TV shows with binary sarcasm labels
The baseline features specified are MFCC-20, indicating 20 MFCCs as the reference representation
The downstream model is a fixed RBF SVM with C=1.6 and gamma=0.0065, requiring fixed-dimensional numeric input
Sarcasm in speech is often conveyed through prosodic cues such as pitch variation, energy contour, and speaking rate
Simple frame-level features aggregated via summary statistics produce fixed-dimensional vectors compatible with SVM input
avoid_repeating: No prior rounds exist; nothing to avoid repeating
risks: Small dataset (690 samples) may cause high variance in 5-fold CV, making it hard to distinguish candidate quality
Simple summary statistics may lose important temporal dynamics of sarcasm prosody
TV show audio may contain background noise or music that degrades acoustic feature quality
Fixed SVM hyperparameters were likely tuned for MFCC-20 and may not be optimal for other feature dimensionalities
Some candidates produce different dimensionalities which may interact differently with the fixed gamma parameter

round_summary.overall_hypothesis: Building on Round 0 evidence that MFCC-20+delta+delta-delta (120-dim, 0.712 F1) is the strongest representation and that higher-order MFCCs and temporal dynamics both contribute, this round tests four refinement directions around the MFCC-delta backbone—richer aggregation, extended coefficient count, MFCC+prosody fusion, and temporal segmentation—plus two exploratory candidates targeting spectral representations not yet tested (chroma and spectral bandwidth/centroid/rolloff ensemble).
evidence_used: MFCC-20+delta+delta-delta mean/std (120-dim) achieved 0.712 F1, +0.010 over baseline, indicating temporal dynamics of spectral envelope encode sarcasm-relevant modulation.
MFCC-20 > MFCC-13 by +0.015 F1, suggesting higher-order coefficients carry non-redundant spectral detail; extending beyond 20 may yield further gains.
All round-0 candidates used mean/std or basic summary-stat aggregation; richer aggregation (percentiles, slope) was identified as an untested direction.
Prosodic features (pitch, energy) performed poorly standalone but were never tested as supplements to a strong MFCC backbone.
Spectral contrast (14-dim, 0.654) was the strongest non-MFCC family but still weak; other spectral descriptors (chroma, spectral centroid/bandwidth/rolloff) remain untested.
Fixed gamma=0.0065 may disadvantage very low-dim features; fusion candidates maintain moderate dimensionality to reduce this confounder.
avoid_repeating: MFCC-20 mean/std only (40-dim) — this is the fixed baseline.
MFCC-13 mean/std only (26-dim) — tested as cand05, underperformed.
Pitch F0 summary stats alone (9-dim) — tested as cand02, very weak.
Energy RMS summary stats alone (8-dim) — tested as cand03, weak.
Pitch+energy combined alone (9-dim) — tested as cand06, weak and partially redundant.
Spectral contrast mean/std alone (14-dim) — tested as cand04, weak.
MFCC-20+delta+delta-delta mean/std (120-dim) — tested as cand01, already best known.
risks: Extending MFCC count to 25-30 may capture noise in higher cepstral coefficients, especially with 690 samples and fixed gamma.
Richer aggregation increases dimensionality substantially; the fixed gamma=0.0065 may not be optimal for the new feature scale, potentially masking true feature quality.
Fusion candidates combining MFCC backbone with prosodic supplements increase dimensionality where the added features were individually weak; the marginal benefit may be negligible.
Segment-level temporal aggregation (first-half vs second-half) doubles dimensionality and assumes sarcastic prosody has temporal asymmetry, which may not hold for short utterances.
Exploratory spectral candidates (chroma, spectral shape descriptors) have no prior evidence in this pipeline and may underperform like spectral contrast did.

round_summary.overall_hypothesis: Round 2 targets four evidence-grounded directions from the Round 1 winner (MFCC-20 rich 7-stat aggregation, 140-dim, F1=0.729): (1) ablation of which aggregation statistics carry the sarcasm signal (skew/kurtosis vs min/max/median), (2) controlled addition of delta features on top of rich aggregation at moderate dimensionality, (3) fusion of the best representation with prosodic summary features, and (4) an exploratory temporal-regression approach that encodes MFCC trajectory slope per coefficient as an alternative to delta features. The goal is to determine whether the 0.729 result can be pushed further by targeted enrichment or whether it is near ceiling for this SVM configuration, while also identifying which aggregation components are load-bearing to guide future compaction.

All candidates keep total dimensionality in the 130–180 range where the fixed RBF SVM gamma=0.0065 appears to perform well, informed by the observation that 154-dim outperformed 180-dim and 300-dim representations.

round_summary.overall_hypothesis: Round 4 focuses on four refinement directions around the current best (cand31, MFCC-20 7-stat + SC 5-stat, 175-dim, F1=0.7438): (1) testing whether a compact 6-stat MFCC backbone (dropping skew) with enriched spectral contrast can match or exceed cand31 at lower dimensionality; (2) probing whether deeper 7-stat spectral contrast aggregation adds further sub-band timbral signal on a compact backbone within the ~170-dim sweet spot; (3) isolating the delta MFCC temporal variability signal via a std-only 20-dim supplement that avoids the dimensionality penalty seen in earlier delta attempts; (4) retesting prosody with a voiced-only F0 computation (excluding unvoiced-as-zero artifacts) as a minimal supplement to the strongest known configuration; and (5) an exploratory test of zero-crossing rate as an untested complementary voicing/texture feature. All candidates are designed to stay within 145-180 dimensions to respect the gamma=0.0065 dimensionality ceiling identified in Rounds 2-3.

round_summary.overall_hypothesis: Round 5 pursues three evidence-grounded refinement directions and two controlled exploratory supplements. First, it tests whether MFCC kurtosis is dispensable (like skew was confirmed dispensable in Rounds 3-4), which would reveal the minimal effective MFCC aggregation set. Second, it tests the minimal effective spectral contrast aggregation (3-stat vs 5-stat). Third, it tests alternative spectral supplements (spectral flatness and spectral rolloff) individually on the MFCC backbone — these were only tested as part of a weak standalone ensemble (cand16, Round 1) but have never been isolated as small supplements on the strong 140-dim MFCC backbone the way spectral contrast was. Fourth, it tests a combined compact backbone with both SC and spectral flatness. Fifth, it tests log mel band energies from selected sub-bands as an exploratory supplement, hypothesizing that band-specific spectral energy patterns lost in the MFCC cepstral compression may carry complementary sarcasm-discriminative information. All candidates stay within the 135-165 dim safe zone identified in Rounds 3-4.

round_summary.overall_hypothesis: Round 6 targets the remaining micro-optimization space around the history-best cand31 (MFCC-20 7-stat + SC 5-stat, 175-dim, F1=0.7438). Three candidates perform controlled SC aggregation ablations to identify which SC extremum (min vs max) carries the residual signal identified in Round 5's cand52 comparison. One candidate tests whether finer temporal resolution in the MFCC/SC extraction (hop_length=256 vs default 512) yields more stable aggregation statistics and better captures fast prosodic modulation. One exploratory candidate tests inclusion of the zeroth cepstral coefficient (C0, log-energy) alongside a compact MFCC backbone, probing whether explicit overall energy information — distinct from the energy implicitly spread across higher MFCCs — adds complementary signal. The round is designed to either squeeze a small final gain from the MFCC+SC configuration or confirm the optimization ceiling.

round_summary.overall_hypothesis: Round 8 probes whether the cand71 configuration (C0-C20 6-stat no-skew + SC 4-stat mean/std/median/min, 154-dim, F1=0.7524) can be further improved through three directions: (1) aggregation enrichment with explicit range statistics that capture excursion magnitude, motivated by the R7 finding that raw min/max outperform percentiles; (2) controlled SC compression to isolate SC median's contribution in the C0-present context; (3) exploration of two untested compact feature families—harmonics-to-noise ratio (HNR) and energy-derivative dynamics—as minimal supplements on the cand71 backbone, targeting voice quality and emphasis pattern dimensions not covered by MFCC spectral shape or SC timbral contrast. Two additional candidates test spectral bandwidth as a minimal supplement (previously only tested standalone in R1 where it failed) and a sub-band energy ratio proxy for vocal effort. All candidates stay within the 145–175 dim sweet spot identified across rounds 3–7.

round_summary.overall_hypothesis: Round 8 identified RMS energy first-derivative dynamics (3-dim) as the first non-MFCC/non-SC supplement to produce a positive delta (+0.0059), yielding a new history best (cand85, F1=0.7583, 157-dim).
